title: The tail call inside a function applied where it is written (`e |> fun a -> f a`) is lost when the caller allocates locally
summary: `e |> fun a -> loop (n - 1) a` as the last expression of a function that allocates on the local stack (here a comparison of two tuples) does not run in constant stack in native code; so do `(fun a -> ...) @@ e` and `(fun m a -> ...) n e`. Bytecode and OCaml 5.4.0 run it in constant stack.
cause: `simplify_lets` in `lambda/simplif.ml` (with `beta_reduce`) puts the body of the applied function in place of the application and drops its `Rc_close_at_apply` mark, so the call in the body becomes a plain call at the end of the caller's region.

fix.text: Puts the reduced body under `Lexclave` when the application was marked to end the region before the call. Builds; `test.ml` then prints the expected result; testsuite unchanged.
